prompt: What does `handle` receive besides the request's `event`?
hint: It is what does SvelteKit's own work.

choices.text: The response, ready to be sent
choices.why: The response is what `resolve` returns.

choices.text: The data the layouts' load functions returned for the page
choices.why: Load functions run inside `resolve`, after `handle` starts.

choices.text: `resolve`, which does what SvelteKit would have done anyway
choices.why: Right: code before it runs first, code after it sees the response.

choices.text: The page component, already rendered
choices.why: Nothing is rendered until `resolve` runs.

prompt: Which file holds the planner's `handle`?
hint: It runs on the server only.

choices.text: `src/hooks.server.js`
choices.why: Right: SvelteKit looks for that name.

choices.text: `vite.config.js`
choices.why: That configures the build; it is not called per request.

choices.text: `src/routes/+layout.server.js`
choices.why: That holds a load function, not hooks.

choices.text: `src/hooks.js`
choices.why: That one runs in both places, and has no `handle`.

prompt: Why did the first version of the log break `npm run build`?
hint: About is prerendered.

choices.text: `console.log` is not allowed in a hook
choices.why: The second version logs too.

choices.text: `performance.now()` does not exist on the server
choices.why: Node has it; the error named `url.search`.

choices.text: The hook was in the wrong file and was imported by the browser
choices.why: The file was right; the build ran it.

choices.text: It read `url.search` while About was being prerendered
choices.why: Right: a build-time request has no real query, and SvelteKit refuses it.

prompt: The value from `$app/env` that is true while the build prerenders is called ___.
hint: A word ending in -ing.

prompt: After the week page, a click on Guitar and a session added, which lines did the log show? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three trips to the server, and only three.

choices.text: `GET /`
choices.why: Yes: the first page.

choices.text: A `POST` to `?week=…&/add`, answered 200
choices.why: Yes: `use:enhance` got JSON back.

choices.text: A `GET` for the click on Guitar
choices.why: That needed nothing from the server.

choices.text: A `GET /about`
choices.why: About was not visited, and it is a file anyway.

prompt: Match each header with what it asks the browser.
hint: One is about frames, one about guessing, one about links.

pairs.right: Trust the declared type, do not guess
Keep the address from other sites
Never show the page in another site's frame

prompt: With `handle = sequence(log, headers)`, put what happens to one request in order.
hint: Each one wraps the ones after it.
trap: Printing first would measure nothing, since nothing has happened yet.

prompt: Why did `curl -I /about` show none of the three headers?
hint: Who answered that request?

choices.text: `sequence` only runs its last function for pages without data
choices.why: `sequence` runs every function, every time.

choices.text: It is a prerendered file, sent without SvelteKit
choices.why: Right: the adapter serves files itself, and no hook sees them.

choices.text: `csr = false` pages may not carry headers
choices.why: Page options say nothing about headers.

choices.text: `curl -I` asks for the headers of the dev server instead
choices.why: It asked the built server, on port 3000.

prompt: Why is `Content-Security-Policy` harder to set by hand than the other three?
hint: Think of the small script in every page.

choices.text: It would block the stylesheet that every page links to, so no page could be styled
choices.why: A policy can allow the site's own styles.

choices.text: SvelteKit puts an inline script in every page, which the policy must allow
choices.why: Right: its own `csp` option marks those scripts.

choices.text: Browsers ignore it on localhost
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: It can only be sent from a prerendered page
choices.why: Prerendered pages are the ones hooks cannot touch.

prompt: What is `event.locals`?
hint: It lives as long as one request.

choices.text: Settings read from the `.env` file
choices.why: Environment variables are something else.

choices.text: A store shared by every request the server answers
choices.why: Each request gets its own; sharing is what lesson 11 warned against.

choices.text: Variables the browser keeps for the page
choices.why: It is the server's and never reaches the browser on its own.

choices.text: An object for one request, which hooks write and loads read
choices.why: Right: written once, read by everything after.

prompt: Why does the planner give each request a short id?
hint: Where does the id appear?

choices.text: To match a log line with the page somebody saw
choices.why: Right: the same id is in both.

choices.text: So the server can refuse a request it has answered once
choices.why: Each id is new and nothing checks it.

choices.text: So that the browser can cache each page under its own name
choices.why: It is not sent as a cache key.

choices.text: To sign the session cookie
choices.why: The planner has no session.

prompt: A page needs a value a hook computed. Where should it come from?
hint: `locals` never reaches the browser by itself.

choices.text: From a global variable the hook sets
choices.why: A global is shared by every request.

choices.text: From a cookie the hook writes
choices.why: That goes to the browser, not into the page's data.

choices.text: From what a load function returns, reading `locals`
choices.why: Right: what a page needs goes in a load's result.

choices.text: From `event.locals`, read in the component
choices.why: Components cannot see `locals`.

prompt: Match each `kind` with where its error came from.
hint: Only one of them is a surprise.

pairs.right: SvelteKit's own, such as no route

prompt: Without `handleError`, what did the visitor see when the data file was missing?
hint: SvelteKit's safe default.

choices.text: A blank page
choices.why: The error page was rendered.

choices.text: A 404, because the file could not be found
choices.why: A missing file on the server is the server's failure, a 500.

choices.text: The `ENOENT` message and the file's path
choices.why: That went to the server's terminal only.

choices.text: A 500 with "Internal Error"
choices.why: Right: nothing from the error itself.

prompt: Why must `handleError` never throw?
hint: When does it run?

choices.text: Because a hook must always return a response
choices.why: `handleError` returns an object, not a response.

choices.text: It runs because something already failed; its own error has nowhere to go
choices.why: Right: keep it to logging and building an object.

choices.text: Because a throw would show the stack to the visitor
choices.why: SvelteKit never shows that; the problem is what happens next.

choices.text: Because throwing there restarts the server
choices.why: The lesson says nothing like that.

prompt: After `handleError` was added, why did `/courses/piano` still say "There is no course called “piano”"?
hint: Who raised that 404?

choices.text: It is `kind: 'app'`, and the hook returns those unchanged
choices.why: Right: only `'unknown'` errors get the plain sentence.

choices.text: Because a 404 never reaches the hook
choices.why: It reaches it, with `kind: 'app'`.

choices.text: Because the course page has its own error page
choices.why: There is one `+error.svelte`, at the root.

choices.text: Because `piano` matched no route at all
choices.why: It matched the course route; the load raised it.

prompt: What status did the planner answer with while `data/planner.json` was moved away?
hint: Internal Error.

prompt: Match each hook with the file it lives in.
hint: `hooks.js` runs on both sides.

prompt: What does `handleFetch` sit in front of?
hint: Only one side's requests.

choices.text: Every `fetch` made in the browser after the first page has loaded
choices.why: It is a server hook.

choices.text: Requests for prerendered files
choices.why: No hook sees those.

choices.text: Every `fetch` a load or action makes on the server
choices.why: Right: it can send them to a faster internal address.

choices.text: Every request the browser sends to the server
choices.why: That is `handle`.

prompt: With `reroute` sending `/sobre` to `/about`, what does the address bar show?
hint: It changes the route, not the address.

choices.text: Nothing, until the page has loaded
choices.why: The browser shows what was asked for.

choices.text: `/about`, after a redirect
choices.why: No redirect happens.

choices.text: `/sobre`
choices.why: Right: the address stays as typed.

choices.text: Both, one after the other
choices.why: Nothing moves the address.

prompt: What does `transport` make possible that lesson 13 could not do?
hint: Lesson 13 tried to return a function.

choices.text: Sending a class of your own whose state is data
choices.why: Right: the data travels and the constructor runs again.

choices.text: Skipping the check that forbids reading the query during prerendering
choices.why: That is `building`, in another section.

choices.text: Returning functions from a server load
choices.why: It does not make functions travel.

choices.text: Running a server load in the browser
choices.why: A server load never leaves the server.

prompt: Every response must say who served it, in an `X-Served-By` header. Where does that go?
hint: Every response, including the files.

choices.text: In `handleFetch`
choices.why: That is for the server's own `fetch` calls.

choices.text: In a `handle`, and in whatever serves the prerendered files
choices.why: Right: hooks never see the files.

choices.text: In each page's `+page.server.js`
choices.why: Pages without one, and files, would miss it.

choices.text: In `handleError`
choices.why: That runs only for errors.

prompt: A visitor writes in quoting reference `d1afdf92`. What do you look for?
hint: The id is in two places.

choices.text: The browser's console on your own computer
choices.why: The error happened on the server.

choices.text: A file of that name under `build/`, the one the error page was rendered from
choices.why: The id names a request, not a file.

choices.text: The session with that id in the data file
choices.why: Sessions have numbers; this is a request.

choices.text: The server's log lines that start with `d1afdf92`
choices.why: Right: the failure and its request, together.
